answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The mirror multiplier is published, charged in beacon, and zenith lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1578 identities would post 2783 proofs and burn roughly 18 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
